newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik prisoner exchange delayed, says U.N..
newsitem.headline: Tajik prisoner exchange delayed, says U.N..

text.p: The United Nations on Tuesday said an exchange of prisoners of war and detainees in the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan had been delayed, in a setback for a hard-won peace deal.

"They (Tajik government and armed Islamic opposition) agreed to carry out the exchange on 18 and 19 July 1997 in order to allow effective finalisation of necessary organisational (matters)," U.N. military observers based in the Tajik capital Dushanbe said in a statement made available to reporters.
Under a peace accord signed last month, ending a four-year civil war, the government and opposition were meant to have swapped a first batch of 50 prisoners before Tuesday.
The issue of prisoner exchanges threatened at one point to scupper the peace accord, signed in Moscow after months of tortuous negotiations.
A senior U.N. official, who declined to be named, told Reuters the reason for the delay was an opposition demand for particular prisoners.
"The opposition are demanding not just any fighters but particular individuals," the official said.
The government is believed to hold around 500-600 opposition fighters, while the guerrillas are said to hold about 2,000 government troops.
The war in the far-flung Central Asian state of 5.7 million, bordering Afghanistan and China, claimed tens of thousands of lives. A ceasefire has held since December last year.
